newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM SEEKING MORE PARTS SUPPLIERS IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: GM SEEKING MORE PARTS SUPPLIERS IN HUNGARY.

text.p: U.S. automaker General Motors Corp said on Tuesday it had started exploring additional cooperation with Hungary's auto parts industry.
"There's plenty of opportunity," GM Europe President Richard Donnelly told a news conference. "Today we identified broad areas of cooperation, and we put into place (committees) to study them."

Donnelly arrived in Hungary on Monday for two days of meetings with government officials, including Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and Industry Minister Szabolcs Fazakas. The talks were aimed at increasing GM's involvment in the country's parts business, Donnelly said.
Coooperation could extend into research and development as well as new contracts to supply GM with parts, but no plans for additional GM investment in Hungary were discussed, he said.
Donnelly added that the committees would meet periodically, but he offered no details about the next set of talks.
GM, which has invested 700 million marks in Hungary to assemble cars and manufacture engines, bought roughly 200 million marks of Hungarian auto parts in 1996, Donnelly said.
The automaker's plans to boost parts purchases in Hungary are part of a goal to buy $1.0 billion worth of parts a year in central Europe by 2000, he said.
